headline: Automated Hub Shifts Allentown Prescription Work
so_what: Walgreens opened a robotic micro-fulfillment center in Allentown, PA, projected to support ~650 stores and ~29M prescriptions a year; its network now counts 15 centers supporting 5,500+ stores and 18M prescriptions a month. Picking and packing move from stores to automated hubs, a hybrid pharmacist role (store + centralized) is rolling out in six states, and human pharmacists still handle controlled substances and time-sensitive fills. Point-of-care scanning is being opened to non-specialists — the sonographer’s defensible ground is complex studies, quality assurance and training others.

headline: Data Centers Crowd Out Ordinary Work – The Impact of Labor Shortage
so_what: Electrical Trends’ field research: data-center builds are absorbing scarce electricians — electrical work is 45–70% of a typical data-center construction budget (IBEW) and the hardest trade to staff; training programs produce about 55 workers per 100 needed, construction wages are rising ~5–5.5% a year, and ordinary projects in Texas and Virginia are slowing because crews are tied up on data centers. Demand and pricing power sit with licensed electricians who can staff or lead these crews.
reason: data centers are absorbing electricians faster than training replaces them — wages and pricing power are rising for licensed crews

Scarce QS capacity keeps its pricing power through a soft patch; margin pressure, not headcount, is the near-term risk.
